7.text: The Chukchee are well built and healthy, though rather heavy; so that

8.text: the saddle-reindeer bought from the Lamut frequently prove too weak for

9.text: their new masters. Nor are the Chukchee as nimble of foot as are the Lamut

10.text: hunters. Stout people, however, are rare. I met only one who was rather

11.text: portly, and on this account he received the nickname Um-Kutuˊwg̣i; i. e.,

11.note: Tier-1 nickname. Stress ˊ (U+02CA) after "Kutu", g carries dot below (U+0323), confirmed at 4x against machine text's straight apostrophe substitute; no plain g anywhere on this line to contrast against but the dot is plainly visible under g in both occurrences (lines 11 and 12).

13.text: The hands and feet, as with all tribes of Arctic Asia, are small. The

14.text: young men of the Reindeer division sweat copiously upon slight exertion, —

15.text: for instance, while running about the herd, — and on this account the Reindeer

16.text: Chukchee call themselves, half facetiously, “the sweating-people” (gɪʟ̣oˊta-raˊmkɪn).
16.resolved: gɪʟ̣oˊta-raˊmkɪn = g + ɪ U+026A + ʟ U+029F + U+0323 + o + stress U+02CA + t + a + hyphen + r + a + stress U+02CA + m + k + ɪ U+026A + n
16.note: Tier-1 self-designation, hyphenated compound with one stress mark per member (cf. keying_spec.md §5.1's ᵋy-qaˊa-raˊmkɪt pattern for two stresses in one hyphenated compound — two roots, two stresses is not a culminative-stress violation). Leading g confirmed bare (no dot below) at 4x, contrasted against the dotted g in wg̣i on lines 11/12 on the same page. The lateral after ɪ is small-cap ʟ with dot below (ʟ̣, §2.2's four-lateral series l/ḷ/ʟ/ʟ̣), confirmed at 4x.

17.text: Many of the women are clumsily shaped, with short waists, and legs out of

18.text: proportion to the rest of their bodies. Some of the Chukchee have consider-

19.text: able physical strength, especially the reindeer-breeders, who have a superior

20.text: diet. I saw men who were able to carry a whole reindeer-carcass on their
20.note: Machine text (mz/ocr) read this as "carçass" with a spurious cedilla; confirmed at 4x it is plain "carcass", ordinary c.

21.text: backs for a quarter of a mile, or lift a great stone about two hundred pounds

22.text: in weight. The younger Chukchee are continually bent on increasing their

23.text: physical powers by lifting and carrying stones, by running foot-races for long

24.text: distances, etc. The Maritime Chukchee and the Eskimo even have special

25.text: lifting-stones for each man. These are picked up among the crumbling rocks,

26.text: and are usually cylindrical in shape, with smooth surfaces. One of my European

27.text: fellow-travellers, however, was able to surpass all the men of the villages

28.text: between Mariinsky Post and Indian Point in a hand-pulling contest.

29.text: The cheek-bones of the Chukchee are much less prominent than those

30.text: of the Tungus or Yakut; their noses are often large, well-shaped, and even

31.text: aquiline, though noses with the low Mongolian bridge are also frequently met

33.text: Many Chukchee have faces that are clumsy in outline, flat skulls, and

34.text: low straight foreheads, while the lower part of the face is disproportionately

35.text: large and strong.¹ A handsome head is frequently compared to a round

36.text: grassy hummock. In their tales, man is sometimes called “hummocky-head.”
